title: structured output: add constrained decoding backends (CFG, regex) + tokenizer edge-case handling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Structured output (JSON/tuple-like responses, function/tool-calling outputs) is critical for downstream consumers. Free-form decoding results in hallucinations and post-processing flakiness. This PR introduces two constrained decoding backends (CFG/grammar-based and regex-constrained emitters) and fixes tokenizer edge cases that caused invalid structured tokens to be emitted in streaming and re-runs.

Summary: Implemented backend abstractions for constrained decoding, integrated into the OpenAI-compat streaming path and the new structured_output flag. Provides: (1) CFG backend that enforces a context-free grammar via partial-derivation constraints at token-level; (2) Regex backend for simpler patterns where grammar is overkill; (3) Tokenizer-aware constraint mapper that handles subword/split-token boundaries and byte-level encodings to avoid producing truncated JSON tokens mid-token; (4) Streaming stability improvements to ensure constraints are respected across chunk boundaries and reconnects; (5) Updates to OpenAI compatibility layer to expose structured_output modes and fallback policies.

Design notes: The constrained decoding API is pluggable: ConstrainedDecoder is an interface with implementations CFGDecoder and RegexDecoder. Each exposes: initialize(context, prefix_tokens), suggest_allowed_token_ids(tokenizer_state) and update_state(chosen_token). The CFGDecoder keeps a compact LR-like state (internally serialized as strings) so it can be checkpointed in the streaming protocol. The tokenizer-aware layer maps UTF-8 byte sequences to token ids and exposes a small lookahead window to avoid accepting tokens that would split a required token (e.g. '\"' or 'escaped' sequences). We opted for conservative acceptance: if a token would create an invalid prefix according to grammar or regex, it is treated as disallowed.

Compatibility: OpenAI-compat layer now accepts structured_output: {mode: "cfg"|"regex"|"none", grammar: "<SPDX>", pattern: "^\\{.*\\}$", partial_tokens: true}. For clients that request structured_output over stream, the server attaches a compact constraint checkpoint to the stream metadata so reconnects resume with the same constraint state. Backward compatibility: default is "none".

Testing: Added unit tests for CFG parsing, token-boundary cases (multi-byte unicode, tokenizer splits, sentencepiece edgecases), streaming reconnect recovery, and integration tests that exercise function-calling with structured_output enabled. Benchmarks show a 4-6% CPU overhead on decode for CFG constraints on typical prompts (with tight grammars it's higher); perf team suggests further optimization later.

Checklist: - [x] Implements decoders and tokenizer mapping - [x] Integrates with OpenAI-compat streaming code path - [x] Adds unit/integration tests - [x] Adds docs + examples in redwood-docs - [x] Adds metrics (constraint_accept_rate, constraint_reject_count)

Related: Linear ENG-1124 (structured output decoder), PM-248 (product spec).

Asha Patel: Added async compile in cfg_decoder.go (compiles in goroutine and returns a ready flag). Added constraint_rejection_rate metric and unit tests for concurrency. See commits b2d5e7f and g712f3e.

Asha Patel: Addressed in token_boundary_mapper.go, added lookahead and conservative acceptance for split tokens. Updated streaming checkpoint metadata to include tokenizer offset checkpoint.
Evan Brooks: Integration tests look good. One nit: update docs to show example of a regex pattern that forces top-level object only.

release_notes: Adds server-side constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) and tokenizer-aware mapping for reliable structured output. Exposes structured_output options in OpenAI-compat layer. Streaming reconnection preserves constraint state. Metrics added: constraint_accept_rate, constraint_reject_count. Backward compatible; default behavior unchanged.
